nodes.label: Cache-Aside Pattern
nodes.rationale: Cache-aside chosen for video metadata reads: app checks Redis first, falls back to PostgreSQL on miss, then populates the cache. Provides ~10x read speedup on cache hit. TTL of 5 minutes balances freshness vs performance. Cache invalidation on PUT/DELETE ensures consistency.

nodes.label: Database Read Replication
nodes.rationale: Read replica added to scale read-heavy workloads. Repository layer routes writes to primary, reads to replica. Fallback logic added so if replica goes down, reads fall back to primary — teaches replication lag and failover tradeoffs firsthand.

nodes.label: Kafka Chosen Over RabbitMQ
nodes.rationale: Kafka replaces RabbitMQ throughout because Kafka is more commonly asked about in system design interviews. Kafka supports message replay and dead-letter topics, enabling the async video processing pipeline and notification fan-out scenarios.

nodes.label: Consistent Hashing for DB Sharding
nodes.rationale: Consistent hashing ring implemented to distribute video IDs across PostgreSQL shards. When a new shard is added, only ~1/3 of keys need to move (not all), unlike naive modulo hashing — teaches hot shard and rebalancing strategies.

nodes.label: Fan-Out on Read vs Write
nodes.rationale: Pull model (fan-out on read) is slow at scale due to querying all followed creators. Push model (fan-out on write) pre-computes Redis feed lists for fast reads. Hybrid chosen: push for normal users, pull for celebrities (>10K followers) to avoid write amplification.

nodes.label: Redis Pub/Sub for Cross-Server Comments
nodes.rationale: WebSocket connections are stateful and server-local. Redis Pub/Sub bridges multiple server instances: on new comment, publish to channel comments:{videoId}; each server subscribes and pushes to its local WebSocket clients — key insight for real-time chat system interviews.

nodes.label: Sliding Window Rate Limiting via Redis
nodes.rationale: Sliding window counter implemented with Redis INCR + EXPIRE. Applied at 100 req/min per IP (general) and 10 uploads/hour per user. Returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After header. Chosen over token bucket for simplicity; trade-offs documented.
nodes.norm_label: sliding window rate limiting via redis

nodes.label: Flyway SQL Migrations Convention
nodes.rationale: All schema changes go in src/main/resources/db/migration/ as Flyway V{n}__{description}.sql files. Flyway runs automatically on startup, ensuring schema and code stay in sync across environments without manual intervention.

nodes.label: Horizontal Scaling — Stateless API Behind Load Balancer
nodes.rationale: Three stateless Spring Boot instances (app-1, app-2, app-3) run behind Nginx. Round-robin and least_conn strategies compared. Statelessness (no in-process session state) is required for horizontal scaling — any instance can serve any request.
nodes.norm_label: horizontal scaling — stateless api behind load balancer

nodes.label: Dead-Letter Topic (DLQ) for Failed Processing
nodes.rationale: Permanently failed video processing jobs and failed notifications are routed to a dead-letter Kafka topic. Consumer crash mid-processing restarts and replays from Kafka — demonstrates at-least-once delivery semantics and the need for idempotent consumers.
